title: Install the GPU
task: installing a graphics card and identifying its power connections
setting: A white open PC case sits on a labeled anti-static work mat amid component boxes, scissors, pliers, and a screwdriver. The builder unboxes an XFX Speedster SWFT 319 Radeon RX 6800 triple-fan card and fits it into the motherboard PCIe slot from a first-person view.

steps.detail: Hands open the XFX SWIFT 319 retail box, lift the inner lid, and take the triple-fan GPU out of its foam tray.
steps.expected: Case must already be prepped (slot covers removed) and anti-static grounding applied BEFORE unboxing; unboxing itself is otherwise the correct first handling step

steps.text: Inspect both sides of the GPU
steps.detail: The builder holds the card up to show the three fans, flips it to reveal the metal backplate, then brings it near the open white case.
steps.expected: Inspection is correct; power-connector identification must occur during this inspection, not later

steps.text: Remove the rear PCIe slot covers
steps.detail: With a screwdriver on the rear I/O panel, the builder loosens the slot-cover screws and pulls the blanking plates out of the chassis.
steps.expected: Removing slot covers is required but must be completed BEFORE unboxing or handling the GPU; doing so afterward is out of order

steps.text: Orient the GPU at the case opening
steps.detail: The card is held beside the case and turned so its rear bracket faces the open slot-cover gap and the PCIe edge faces the motherboard.
steps.expected: Orientation is correct once covers are removed and the card has been inspected

steps.text: Line the PCIe edge up with the x16 slot
steps.detail: A hand reaches inside to clear the path, then both hands guide the long edge of the GPU toward the motherboard slot through the lower case opening.
steps.expected: Alignment with the x16 slot is correct at this stage

steps.detail: The builder holds up a PCIe power-cable end, then shows the power sockets on the side of the card with an on-screen close-up of the connector pins.
steps.expected: Power connectors must be identified during initial inspection BEFORE any alignment or insertion; performing identification after lining up the card is out of order

steps.text: Press the GPU level into the PCIe slot
steps.detail: Both hands push the graphics card straight into the motherboard x16 slot until it sits flush across the lower case opening.
steps.expected: Full seating into the slot is correct, yet the bracket must then be screwed down immediately and only afterward are the power cables attached

afterClip: Screw down the GPU bracket and plug the PCIe power cables into the card
procedure: Power off and unplug the PC, then ground yourself with an anti-static wrist strap on the anti-static mat
Remove the PCIe slot blanking plates for the target x16 slot before handling the GPU
Unbox the GPU and inspect both sides for damage while identifying the exact power connector types and pin layout required
Confirm the PSU has matching free PCIe power cables
Orient the GPU so the bracket aligns with the rear chassis openings and the edge connector with the motherboard x16 slot
Insert the GPU straight into the slot with even pressure until fully seated and the retention clip engages
Secure the rear bracket to the chassis with the appropriate screws
Connect the identified PCIe power cables firmly to the GPU power sockets
